messages:
ava: heads-up: after running the new MSI on WSL2 i hit two weird DX things: installer put redwoodctl into /usr/local/bin via linuxbrew but my old shim at /home/ava/.local/bin/redwoodctl still exists and gets picked up first in PATH. then the device-code auth flow fails with a 403 redirect mismatch. anyone seen this combo?

diego: oof. which binary is first in `which redwoodctl`?

ava: `which` points to ~/.local/bin/redwoodctl (old copy). but the MSI thought it was installing to /usr/local/bin. i had both on PATH and the shell picked the old one.

marta: installer should detect existing user-local shims and either migrate or warn. we added a symlink step for mac previously, but not for linuxbrew/msi case.

diego: about the 403, what's the exact error? can you paste the device flow output?

ava: snippet: ```
Visit: https://auth.redwood.local/device
Enter code: AB12-CD34
Polling token endpoint...
Error: auth failed: 403 Forbidden (redirect_uri mismatch)
```

marta: redirect_uri mismatch during polling usually means the local redirect the server expects (localhost:xxxx) changed between start and poll, or the binary being used encodes a different client id. if you have two binaries, token endpoint might see different client metadata.

ava: ohhh i bet the old binary was built from an older dev branch with a test client id that our auth server rejects. switching to the new binary makes login succeed.

diego: two fixes: 1) installer should detect existing user-local redwoodctl and prompt to rename/remove or move it to a backup path, 2) add a runtime check in `redwoodctl login` that prints a clear message when device poll returns 403 redirect mismatch, suggesting to `which redwoodctl` and `redwoodctl --version`.

marta: also add a small sanity check: on start of device flow, print the client_id and redirect_uri that will be used (obfuscated) so devs can see mismatch quickly.

infra-bot: Note: package-maintainers pinged for linuxbrew/MSI postinstall migration behavior.

ava: workaround for me: `mv ~/.local/bin/redwoodctl ~/.local/bin/redwoodctl.old` then re-run `redwoodctl login` and it worked. but we should avoid this confusion for new hires.

diego: i'll open INF-3333 to add: postinstall shim migration, preflight `which` check with warning, and improved error message for 403 during device polling. also add docs note about PATH collisions.

ci-bot: Issue created: INF-3333 "redwoodctl: detect user-local shims, postinstall migration, and clearer device-code 403 hints" assigned to @diego.

marta: tiny extra: add `redwoodctl doctor` that verifies binary path, config location, and env vars like HTTPS_PROXY; can be useful for onboarding. low effort.

diego: good idea, adding `doctor` to the ticket as a follow-up.

ava: thanks all. i'll re-test on a clean WSL image once PRs land. tagging: `wsl`, `path`, `device-code`, `installer`, `doctor` :thumbsup:
